chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ibn Jabal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:

We were at his door, then a people came out to us resembling the Zutt. Upon them were waist-wraps and coverings. So we asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about them, and he said: “These are your brothers from the jinn.”

key_terms.الزُّطِّ: the Zutt; a people used here as a point of resemblance in appearance
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, an unseen class of beings

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the jinn visiting Imam Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that a group of beings emerged while the companions were at the door, and Imam Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) identified them as brethren from the jinn. The report indicates the existence of interaction between the jinn and the Imams (عليهم السلام), fitting the chapter theme that they came seeking guidance concerning their religion.
